test(protocol): a test pins PROTOCOL_VERSION, so an added request kind cannot bump it (candybar-step-back-8us0.p1p) (#748)

* test(protocol): a test pins PROTOCOL_VERSION, so an added request kind cannot bump it (candybar-step-back-8us0.p1p)

* test(protocol): the pin's comment names every mirrored spelling and points to the constant for the cost of a bump (candybar-step-back-8us0.p1p)

* test(protocol): the pin's name says it forces a deliberate edit, not that it tells a breaking bump from an additive one (candybar-step-back-8us0.p1p)

refactor(renderer): the host's pushes cross a process, each an adapter input answered by its reply alone (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8rc)

Every reach of the host into the renderer is now an AdapterPush, plain
data checked at build time to cross a process (Crosses<T>), answered by
an AdapterOutput: the reply of the push's own kind, or how it threw.
rendererHost.ask is the one judge of a reply's kind; tell logs a
failure nothing awaits.

- The feed asks for its frame and its lanes, so a frame lands later: a
  wake while it is out is owed the next frame at the spacing, however
  the frame ended, and a subscribe is admitted once its lanes answer,
  opening nothing for one refused or gone meanwhile.
- The pin owns the session's state wake, so the wake lives as long as
  the feed.
- Journal turns are the renderer's. The daemon's close awaits the
  renderer's three teardown steps in today's order, and shutdown awaits
  the close before it exits.
- A render's wait ends when the render cache closes, said as
  ended=closed, so a render the close interrupts holds no timer past it.
- A heap-retainer test draws in a frame of its own, so the suspended
  test frame's registers cannot hold the drawn store.
